preimage.short_description: Removing a $500 million missile-program allocation directive
preimage.compact_description: The amendment would remove a $500million allocation directive for specified Israeli missile-procurement and research/development programs. Removing the directive alone does not establish an overall account-total cut. Domain membership remains an unaccepted proposal.
preimage.meaning: Greene Part A Amendment No.114 to H.R.4016 would delete the whole printed section8067 identified by the exact offered amendment. That section directs one $500million allocation from amounts appropriated under Procurement, Defense-Wide and Research, Development, Test and Evaluation, Defense-Wide, not $500million from each account. It allocates $60million for the Secretary of Defense to provide to the Government of Israel for Iron Dome procurement subject to the named procurement agreement; $127million for the Short Range Ballistic Missile Defense program, including cruise-missile defense research and development; $40million for SRBMD co-production in the United States and Israel; $100million for the upper-tier component, all of that $100million for Arrow3 co-production in the United States and Israel; and $173million for the Arrow System Improvement Program including development of a long-range ground and airborne detection suite. The co-production allocations are subject to the named procurement/co-production agreements and each nation's laws, regulations and procedures as printed. These five amounts total $500million; the upper-tier co-production amount is not a second additional $100million. Deleting this allocation directive does not establish a $500million overall account-total reduction, a ban on all assistance to Israel or repeal of the referenced agreements. It changes this particular direction for the use of amounts under the named accounts; the broader appropriation totals and other authorities are not rewritten by the deletion instruction. The retained complete own offering, resumed recorded question and report identify this exact child and the complete reported section8067 is its target; parent final-passage meaning, geopolitical debate and another domain's conclusion are not used to supply its meaning. The House rejected this amendment on civilJuly18,2025 in the legislativeJuly17Record,6-422with9NotVoting. A Yea supports adopting this exact deletion; a Nay opposes that deletion without establishing a stance on the whole bill or all Israeli assistance. No actual outlay reduction, changed defense capability, program delivery, motive or enactment is inferred. Infrastructure/Technology membership remains an UNACCEPTED candidate proposal: removal of specified missile procurement and explicit research/development allocations is proposed under the existing direct technology/research-governance rule, with independent membership review required before acceptance.
limitations: This is the whole exact section8067deletion, not the whole defense appropriation or an overall-account funding vote. Removing the allocation directive alone does not establish a $500million reduction in total account appropriations.

Preserve all five amounts, the single $100million upper-tier/co-production allocation and the printed agreement/law conditions; no automatic elimination of all Israeli assistance or external agreements is inferred.
Primary binding uses the exact offered/reported child and complete identified reported target. No independent new raw/glyph replay or reconstruction of the entire parent package was performed.
A Nay rejects this particular deletion; it does not establish support for the full package, all foreign military assistance or any motive. Rejection does not establish enactment or actual spending.
Membership is an unaccepted direct technology/R&D allocation proposal requiring independent review; no acceptance, publication, promotion or full-domain authority.
